title: Chaos drills and validation playbook for private deployments
author: Maya R. Singh
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a repeatable, low-risk program of chaos drills and validation tests for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on‑prem). The goal is to validate operational assumptions, SLO resilience, rollback paths, alerting, and runbook accuracy for day‑2 operations without impacting production customers.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to private control plane + runtime bundles shipped to customers (VPC agents and on‑prem installs).
- Intended for staging, pre-prod canary clusters, and a controlled subset of customer sandboxes only.
- Not intended for live customer workloads unless explicit written customer permission and escalation contacts are in place.

Objectives:
1. Exercise and validate: autoscaling, cache warm-up and eviction, KV cache recovery, and model fallback routes.
2. Confirm SLOs and alerting thresholds for latency (p95, p99) and error budget consumption.
3. Verify rollback and de‑flapping procedures for model variants and runtime releases.
4. Ensure on‑call playbooks are accurate and runbook steps succeed under realistic failure modes.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Chaos lead (Engineering Resilience): schedules drills, owns experiment runbooks, and publishes post‑mortem.
- Platform owner (Serving Runtime): provides test harness, model stubs, and failure-injection tooling.
- SRE oncall: executes drill where runbook requires human intervention; verifies incident comms and paging.
- Customer success (when customer sandbox used): obtains approvals and coordinates timeslots.

Preconditions checklist (must pass before any drill):
- Canary/staging cluster isolated from prod traffic: YES/NO
- Backups and snapshot schedule verified (last snapshot < 24h): YES/NO
- Alerting routing configured for drill (suppresses external customer tickets): YES/NO
- Oncall roster and escalation list confirmed: YES/NO
- Observability retention for drill window confirmed (metrics + traces): YES/NO

Minimum safety controls:
- Kill switch: abort command that restores normal routing in < 60s. Example: curl -X POST https://internal-api/controlplane/v1/chaos/abort -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
- Pager suppression window configured in PagerDuty or equivalent; two oncall engineers remain alerted for manual escalation.
- Rate limit of injected failures to 5% of requests for non-blocking experiments.

Standard drill scenarios (examples):
A. GPU preemption spike
  - Intent: Validate autoscaler and model-fallback to CPU-quantized variant.
  - Steps: 1) Mark 20% of GPU nodes as Preempted using fleet emulator. 2) Observe: queue growth, batching behavior, latency p95/p99. 3) Verify automated fallback policy fires and serves from quantized model within 90s.
  - Success criteria: tail latency increase < 2x baseline and requests served with fallback variant with no silent failures.

B. KV cache node loss
  - Intent: Ensure KV-cache warmup and prefix caching do not regress user-visible latency.
  - Steps: 1) Stop KV service on two availability segments. 2) Monitor cold-start token rates and model latency per user. 3) Validate cache priming jobs rehydrate within configured window (default 10m).
  - Success criteria: cold-token fraction returns to baseline within 10m and no auth/consistency errors are raised.

C. Model rollout degraded outputs (regression inject)
  - Intent: Exercise quality‑guardrails and automatic rollback on evaluation regressions.
  - Steps: 1) Deploy a canary model with deliberately lowered ngram precision. 2) Run a predefined prompt-set evaluation (see prompt-sets-and-benchmarks) and compare quality metrics. 3) Verify the Optimize service flags regression and the rollout controller automatically rolls back after configured threshold (e.g., BLEU drop > 12% or Eval score drop > 8%).
  - Success criteria: rollback completes within the configured cooldown window and alerts are created in the regression queue.

D. Network partition (service mesh level)
  - Intent: Validate graceful degradation, fallback regions, and control plane reconnection flows.
  - Steps: 1) Partition network between compute plane and control plane for 3min. 2) Observe request routing, fallback to local cached model weights, and control-plane reconcilers. 3) Verify traffic is routed to a compatible model variant or local cached policy.
  - Success criteria: requests continue with degraded but acceptable latency and automatic reconciliation occurs within 5min.

Experiment definition (YAML example to load into the chaos orchestration tooling):

---
experiment_name: gpu-preempt-sim-2026-02
scope: canary-cluster-east-1
failure_type: node_preempt
percentage: 20
duration_sec: 900
automation_policy: fallback-to-quantized
abort_endpoint: "/controlplane/v1/chaos/abort"
observability_hooks:
  - metrics: "runtime.request.latency.p95"
  - traces: "service:inference-runtime and tag:cache_miss=true"
---

(Notes: fields are strings in this document for readability; load into tooling via the platform CLI.)

Checks, metrics and SLOs to monitor:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per route, alert if p99 > baseline * 2 for >5min.
- Error rate: 4xx/5xx spike detection. Alert if 5xx increases by >1% absolute over baseline
- Queue depth and backlog growth: alert if backlog growth rate > 10 req/s for 3min.
- Eval quality gates: automated eval job results and regression alerts in Optimize feed.

Runbook: step-by-step for a typical GPU-preempt drill (example)
1) Pre-drill validation (15m): confirm preconditions checklist, notify stakeholders in #private-deploy-drills, create drill incident with severity = info.
2) Start experiment via orchestration CLI: 
   redwood-chaos run --experiment gpu-preempt-sim-2026-02 --token $TOKEN
3) Observe metrics for first 2min. If p99 latency > threshold and queue grows rapidly, abort.
4) If automated fallback fails, escalate to platform owner and trigger manual rollback to previous runtime image: 
   redwood-deploy rollback --service inference-runtime --to-tag v2026-01-15 --force
5) After stabilization, run validation suite: convergence of cache, successful inference responses for 500 sampled requests.
6) Post-mortem: publish within 48h including time-to-detect, time-to-recover, which runbook steps failed, and action items.

Post-mortem template (short):
- Summary of what was tested and why
- Timeline (decision log)
- Metrics observed vs expected
- Root cause and contributing factors
- Actions (owner, due date)
- Validation of fixes (how we will re-test)

Frequency and cadence:
- Small drills (single component disruptions): weekly in canary for overall fleet health.
- Larger end-to-end drills (cross-region, control-plane partitions): quarterly.
- Pre-release critical path drills (before major onprem/control-plane releases): mandatory for release windows.

Templates and automation artifacts (where to find them):
- Chaos experiment templates: //git.internal/redwood/chaos-templates (branch: stable).
- CLI tools: redwood-chaos (v1.3+) and redwood-observe (for automated validation).
- Canary config examples: see /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/canary-standup-and-teardown-template (internal doc).

Common failure modes and mitigations (quick reference):
- Slow cold-start after KV loss -> mitigation: increase cache replication factor and reduce priming window to 5m.
- Fallback model too slow -> mitigation: pre-warm quantized variants and tune batching thresholds.
- Alert fatigue during drill -> mitigation: use pager suppression and a dedicated drill incident channel; ensure two humans remain paged.

Operational KPIs to track for program health:
- Drill pass rate (goal >= 90%)
- Mean time to abort (MTTA) for drills with severe regressions (< 3m target)
- Number of runbook edits after drills per quarter (measure of runbook rot)

Appendix: quick commands and examples
- Abort an active experiment: curl -X POST https://internal-api/controlplane/v1/chaos/abort -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"experiment_id":"gpu-preempt-sim-2026-02"}'
- Fetch experiment status: redwood-chaos status --id gpu-preempt-sim-2026-02
- Trigger canary evaluation: redwood-optimize evaluate --prompt-set canary-smoke --model canary-v2 --output artifacts/canary-eval.json

Related pages and references:
- See private-deploy-playbook VPC/onprem for onboarding and safety controls.
- Runtime observability guide for required dashboards and metric names.
- Optimize model regression playbook for evaluation thresholds and auto‑rollback rules.
